source.diagram: Sub-system K2O·SiO2-SiO2 after Kracek [1] and Kracek et al. [2]
source.caption: Atlas text (printed p. 85): 'Fig. 3.117. Sub-system K2O·SiO2-SiO2 after Kracek [1] and Kracek et al. [2]. The additional compound K2O·3SiO2, melting incongruently and reported by Eipeltauer, More [3] is indicated by a dashed line. For the phase equilibria in the SiO2-rich region of the system, with tridymite as a solution phase and not as the polymorph of pure silica, see Wollast [4] and Holmquist [5]. For thermodynamic assessment of the system and calculated phase diagram, see Wu at al. [6].' References: [1] Kracek, F. C.: J. Am. Chem. Soc. 52 (1930), p. 1436/42; [2] Kracek, F. C., N. L. Bowen, G. W. Morey: J. Phys. Chem. 41 (1937) No. 9, p. 1183/93; [3] Eipeltauer, E., A. More: Radex Rundsch. (1960) No. 4, p. 230/8; [4] Wollast, R.: Silicates Ind. 26 (1961) No. 2, p. 89/92; [5] Holmquist, S. B.: J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 44 (1961) No. 2, p. 82/6; [6] Wu, P., G. Eriksson, A. D. Pelton: J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 76 (1993) No. 8, p. 2059/64.

digitization.method: Liquidus traced along the stroke centre (shortest ink path between the junctions, centred across the stroke); invariant lines from the horizontal strokes.
digitization.check: Compound lines (wt% SiO2): K2O·2SiO2 line at 56.0 (stoichiometric 56.1); K2O·4SiO2 line at 71.8 (stoichiometric 71.8). Invariant lines read 741.5 / 769.5 °C (labels 742 / 769). Potassium-disilicate maximum 1046 °C at 56.1 wt% (label 1045). Potassium-tetrasilicate maximum 771 °C at 71.8 wt% (label 770). Potassium-metasilicate liquidus meets the axis at 993 °C (label 976). Silica liquidus meets the axis at 1727 °C (label 1725). Digitized vs printed compositions (wt% SiO2): 45.5 / '45.5', 67.4 / '67.6', 72.5 / '72.5'.
